newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand imposes anti-dumping steel tariff.
newsitem.headline: Thailand imposes anti-dumping steel tariff.

text.p: Thailand has imposed anti-dumping tariffs on steel products from Poland, Russia and Ukraine, a Commerce Ministry official said on Monday.
The official said Thailand started levying the tariff of between 25.29 and 51.90 percent from December 27 on structural steel and hot-rolled sheets from the three countries.
She did not explain how the tariff percentages would be applied.
She said the CIF-based anti-dumping duty will be reviewed in the third quarter of 1997.

The decision followed Thai government studies of dumping allegations by domestic steel firms including structural steel producer Siam Yamato Co Ltd, a unit of Siam Cement Plc, and hot-rolled coil and steel maker Sahaviriya Steel Industries Plc.
The firms charged that steel products from the three countries were dumped in the Thai market at prices below those in their countries of origin.
They alleged that Polish steel products were offered at $250-265 per tonne in Thailand against $500 in Poland.
